verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission successfully launched four astronauts on a 10-day moon journey at 6:35 p.m. EDT on April 1, 2026, from Kennedy Space Center's Pad 39B.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'April 1: NASA Artemis II mission to send four crew on 10-day mission to do a lunar fly-by from KSC’s Launch Pad 39-B at 6:35 p.m.'; R3: '6:35 pm ET April 1, 2026Artemis II liftoff!'; R2: 'Launch: 6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday, April 1, 2026... Launch Pad 39B'; R5: 'lift off from launch pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center... at 6:35 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match on mission, date, time, location (Pad 39B), four astronauts, 10-day moon journey (lunar fly-by), and success confirmed in references.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a 10-day crewed mission orbiting the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA Artemis II mission to send four crew on 10-day mission to do a lunar fly-by'; R2: '10-day flight... around the moon'; R3/R5 confirm crewed, 10-day lunar orbit/flyby.
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported: crewed (four astronauts), 10-day, lunar orbit/fly-by.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests technology for future lunar surface landings.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NASA's Artemis II mission will help pave the way for future crewed lunar exploration missions.'
verifications.reasoning: Supports broader role in lunar program (paving way for exploration/landings), but not explicitly 'tests technology for surface landings'; implied but less precise.
